Describe an output file for the checker

describe_output.Rd

Called in the researcher's script after a file is written. Records what the file shows, which column holds the number of persons, which columns group the table, where the numbers behind a figure are, and what changed since the last request. inspect() reads the descriptions: it checks a table by the columns named here instead of guessing them from the column names, checks the numbers behind a figure, and shows the descriptions to the approver in write_report().

Usage

describe_output(
  file,
  note,
  count = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  changes = NULL,
  dir = "."
)

Arguments

file

Path of the file written, relative to dir.

note

What the file shows, in a sentence or two.

count

For a table: the column with the number of persons per row.

by

For a table: the columns that group it (one row per combination).

data

For a figure: the numbers behind it, as a data frame (written to <figure>_data.csv) or the path of a file in dir that holds them.

changes

What changed since the output was last requested.

dir

The output directory. In trial_run() and real_run() the working directory is the output directory.

Value

The path of the description file, invisibly.

Why it exists

A checker cannot release what they do not understand. OpenSAFELY reports that about 25 % of rejected requests lack context for the output and 10 % lack the data behind a figure (https://docs.opensafely.org/output-checking/). inspect() also has to guess: a count column is found by its name (n, count, ...), and a figure cannot be read at all. A description removes the guesswork.

Where descriptions are kept

All descriptions go into one text file, output_descriptions.dcf, in dir: the working directory, which is the output directory when the script runs in trial_run() or real_run(). Describing a file again replaces its description, so the script can be run again. The file is output too: it is checked and released with the rest, so the note must not mention values of persons.

Figures

A figure cannot be checked automatically, but the numbers behind it can. Give them as data, a data frame such as the one the figure was drawn from: it is written next to the figure as <figure>_data.csv and checked like any table. A figure whose numbers need changes needs changes too; a figure is never approved automatically, because only a person can see whether it shows more than its numbers (single points in a scatter plot, a small bar). Give the counts behind the figure, not row-level data.

See also

Other safe output: safe_count(), safe_model(), safe_summary()

Examples

out <- file.path(tempdir(), "describe_example")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
tab <- safe_count(fake_persons, c("sex", "occupation"))
#> Suppressed 1 cell with fewer than 5 persons, and 3 more so it cannot be worked
#> out from the totals.
write.csv(tab, file.path(out, "sex_occupation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
describe_output("sex_occupation.csv", "Persons by sex and occupation, 2024.",
                count = "n", by = c("sex", "occupation"), dir = out)
inspect(out)
#> <mimic_inspection> 2 files in
#> C:/Users/danie/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpCclG4q/describe_example
#> ℹ Checked without the real data: dominance and text checks are limited.
#> ℹ No register: tables were not compared with earlier releases.
#> ! REVIEW BY HAND: output_descriptions.dcf
#> • Descriptions written by the researcher cannot be searched without the real
#> data; read them for values of persons.
#> ✔ APPROVED: sex_occupation.csv
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 1 approved, 0 need changes, 1 to review by hand.
